ANALYSIS: No fusion trials yet. Single models reach 0.81-0.83 AUROC, with H-optimus-1 best (0.830). Adding metadata to a model gives little benefit or slightly hurts, so age/sex are weak.
REASONING: Start with a strong, simple reference: early fusion with balance_blocks so no model dominates by size, standardised features, and moderate regularisation. In this regime (~134 patients, ~5600 features) small C usually works best for linear probes. meta_weight=1 keeps the weak metadata shrunk. No PCA and no L2 norm, so this is the plain baseline for later knob comparisons.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.83-0.85, a modest gain over H-optimus-1. If it falls below 0.82, early concatenation may be over-parameterised, and next I would test PCA or late fusion, which is less sensitive to dimensionality.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with strong regularisation (C=0.001, balanced blocks) reaches 0.829, roughly equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Concatenating the models therefore adds little at this setting. Lepidic and Papillary are the weakest classes (~0.72-0.74). Late fusion and gated fusion are both untested.
REASONING: This is still the exploration phase, so the next trial should map an untested method. Late fusion with mean_logit is the simplest robust ensemble of three per-model linear classifiers. Averaging models whose errors are partly independent often gives a clear gain with small n. I keep C=0.001 and no PCA so the comparison with trial 1 stays fair.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.835-0.845, with gains on Lepidic and Papillary from ensemble diversity. If it ties trial 1, the models are largely redundant, and later trials should tune C, L2 normalisation and PCA rather than the fusion type.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 with balanced blocks (0.829) matches the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.830), but does not beat it. Late mean_logit is slightly worse. Per-class AUROC shows Lepidic and Papillary as the weak classes (~0.72-0.74). The gated method and the regularisation axis are both still untested.
REASONING: We are in the exploration phase, so mapping the untested gated method is worthwhile. I use a conservative setting suited to 134 training patients per fold: small hidden layer, high dropout, strong weight decay, moderate epochs and lr=0.001. Adding PCA 64 shrinks the input dimension and limits overfitting. L2 normalisation stabilises scale across models.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of roughly 0.80-0.83. If it is clearly below 0.82, I will conclude that gating overfits at this sample size and focus on early/late fusion (C sweep, PCA, stacking). If it reaches about 0.835 or higher, I will explore gated variants further.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 (0.829) matches the best single model, hoptimus1 at 0.830, so fusion adds nothing yet. Late mean_logit and the gated network are slightly worse. Metadata hurts the single models a little, so meta_weight is not the bottleneck. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes (about 0.72-0.74). The main unknowns are regularisation strength and preprocessing (L2 norm, PCA) for early fusion.
REASONING: With 134 training patients and about 5,600 dimensions, the C value matters most. C=0.001 may be over- or under-shrunk. Testing a stronger-shrinkage variant together with L2 normalisation (which helps reduce slide-level scale and batch effects in mean-pooled features) maps an important axis. I keep balance_blocks=True and meta_weight=1 so the comparison stays clean. Exploration budget allows changing two knobs at once, but to stay interpretable I change only l2_normalize while keeping C fixed.
EXPECTED: L2 normalisation should give a small gain, perhaps 0.005-0.01, mostly in Lepidic and Papillary. If it gives no change or a loss, per-slide scale is not informative noise. In that case I will vary C and PCA next instead.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 with balanced blocks (0.829) only matches the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.830). L2 normalisation made no difference. Late mean_logit and the gated net were both slightly worse. Metadata adds little: alone it reaches 0.60, and it slightly hurts single models. The weak classes are Papillary (~0.72) and Lepidic (~0.74).
REASONING: Regularisation strength is the knob most likely to matter, and only C=0.001 has been tried for early fusion. With about 5,600 standardised features and 134 patients, the best C is uncertain. Testing C=0.01 maps one side of the curve, and everything else is held fixed so the result is interpretable.
EXPECTED: If weaker shrinkage lets the complementary signal from the three models through, AUROC should rise to about 0.835-0.84, mainly on Papillary and Lepidic. If it drops, the optimum is at or below 0.001. The next step would then be C=0.0001 or PCA-based dimension reduction rather than looser regularisation.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 (0.829) roughly matches the best single model (hoptimus1, 0.830) but does not beat it. Raising C to 0.01 hurt, so stronger regularisation may help. L2 normalisation had no effect. Late mean_logit and gated fusion were both slightly worse. Metadata hurts or is neutral at the single-model level.
REASONING: The C trend points toward stronger shrinkage, so C=0.0001 is the natural next step for early fusion. PCA is still untested in early fusion, but stronger shrinkage is the cleaner single-knob question. Lowering C on 5600 standardised columns is roughly equivalent to keeping only the dominant shared directions.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.83–0.84 if heavier shrinkage helps. If it drops, the C optimum is near 0.001 and early fusion is capped near the single-model level. In that case the next steps are PCA (32/64) for early fusion and stack or learned_weights for late fusion.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion with C=0.001 (#1) gives 0.829, essentially equal to H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). C is sharply tuned: 0.0001 and 0.01 are both worse, and L2 normalisation makes no difference. Late fusion with mean_logit (0.822) and the gated network (0.823) are slightly worse. Papillary (~0.72) and Lepidic (~0.74) are the weak classes in every method, and no fusion has yet shown a gain from combining models.
REASONING: Still in the exploration phase. The main untested question is whether a learned combination can exploit per-class complementarity between models, given that simple averaging in #2 did not. A stacker on base log-probabilities can learn class-specific model weights, for example trusting Gated for Cribriform or Papillary where it scored higher. I keep the base learners at the best-known C=0.001 and use a moderate stack_C=0.1, because the inner-CV meta-features from about 107 patients are noisy.
EXPECTED: Possible AUROC of about 0.83-0.84, with better Papillary and Micropapillary scores if model errors are complementary. If it comes in at or below 0.829, learned late combination adds nothing at this sample size. Then the remaining hope is early-fusion variants such as PCA, meta_weight or unbalanced blocks, or accepting that fusion matches but does not beat H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion of full embeddings at C=0.001 (0.829) only matches the best single model, H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). The C sweep peaks sharply at 0.001, and L2 normalisation does nothing. Late fusion (mean_logit, stack) and gated fusion were all slightly worse. Metadata adds little: the +meta baselines are no better than the image-only models. Lepidic and Papillary are the weak classes, at about 0.72–0.74.
REASONING: Early fusion is the strongest method, but with about 5600 dimensions and 134 patients it is heavily ridge-shrunk. Per-model PCA inside the fold is the main untested knob. It could remove redundant or noisy directions so each model contributes compact signal, and it lets a weaker penalty work. PCA=32 per model gives 96 features, which suits n=134. With fewer features, C=0.01 is the natural matching regularisation strength. I keep balance_blocks=True and the other settings as in the best trial to isolate the PCA effect.
EXPECTED: If compressing the redundant directions helps, I expect AUROC of about 0.835–0.845, mainly through Lepidic and Papillary. If AUROC drops below 0.825, the discriminative signal is spread across many dimensions that PCA throws away. I would then go back to full-dimension early fusion and test balance_blocks=False or meta_weight next.

ANALYSIS: Fusion has not beaten the best single model: early concatenation at C=0.001 (0.829) only ties H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). L2 normalisation, PCA 32 and other C values change nothing beyond noise, and late fusion (mean_logit, stack) is slightly worse. Metadata slightly hurts single models. The gated model scored 0.823 with the lowest fold SD and the best Cribriform/Papillary AUROC, so it may be complementary but is under-regularised.
REASONING: I am skipping balance_blocks=False because, for unit-variance features, it mostly acts like a C rescaling, and the C sweep already maps that. The most informative remaining exploration trial is a strongly regularised gated model. Using a smaller PCA, a smaller hidden layer, heavier weight decay and fewer epochs targets the overfitting expected with 134 patients per fold. Its per-patient gating is the only mechanism here that could exploit the per-class complementarity between models.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.83-0.84 with low SD, possibly crossing the roughly 0.01 threshold. If it stays at or below 0.825, the gated family is not worth more budget. I would then focus on late learned_weights or early fusion with small PCA, accepting that the models are largely redundant.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at about 0.82-0.83, which is no better than the best single model (hoptimus1 at 0.830). Early fusion with C=0.001 is the most robust; C between 0.001 and 0.01 is flat, while C=0.0001 underfits. L2 norm and PCA make no difference. Metadata adds slightly negatively for single models. Gated and stack are noisier and not better. Untested knobs that could still matter are balance_blocks=False, meta_weight, and the learned_weights combiner, which could down-weight weaker models such as virchow2.
REASONING: In the last exploration slot I want to settle whether block balancing matters. Virchow2 has the most columns (2560) and the weakest single-model AUROC. With balance_blocks=False it would dominate, so this tells us whether the balancing in #1 is helping. The alternative, late learned_weights, is likely close to mean_logit. This cheap test answers a structural question about the early method, which is the current best.
EXPECTED: I expect a small drop in AUROC, perhaps 0.005-0.01, as virchow2 dominates the concatenation. If it instead matches or beats #1, block size does not matter, and the remaining levers are meta_weight and late learned_weights. If it drops clearly, balancing is confirmed as important, and future trials should keep it on.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 (trial #1, 0.829) ties the best single model, hoptimus1 at 0.830; no fusion has clearly beaten it. Late, stacked and gated variants are all slightly worse. Knobs tried so far (L2 norm, PCA 32, block balancing, C 0.0001–0.01) move AUROC by under 0.005 except over-shrinkage at C=0.0001. Metadata alone is weak (0.60), and adding it at weight 1 slightly hurt the single models.
REASONING: Late fusion with mean_logit and stacking underperformed. The untested combiner most likely to help is learned_weights: it can down-weight virchow2, the weakest base model, which mean_logit cannot do. It may also recover the hoptimus1 advantage while still drawing on complementary per-class strengths, such as uni2h/virchow2 on Acinar. Per-model C=0.001 matches the best early setting. This also closes an open question about the late-fusion space.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.828–0.835. If it fails to beat #1 by the threshold, I will conclude that combiner choice does not matter and the three models carry largely redundant signal. I would then probe early fusion with PCA 64/128 or meta_weight before concluding fusion is roughly at the ceiling of hoptimus1.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion (#1, 0.8290) only matches the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8297). Changes to C, L2 normalisation, PCA and balance_blocks all fall within noise, and C=0.001 is clearly the optimum for early fusion. Late fusion is consistently slightly worse, and learned_weights and stack overfit the inner CV. Gated fusion scores lower overall but has a different per-class profile: Cribriform 0.84-0.86 and Papillary up to 0.75, against 0.82 and 0.72 for early fusion. In gated, the heavier regularisation of #9 lowered AUROC relative to #3.
REASONING: The linear early and late variants look saturated, so another small linear tweak is unlikely to clear the 0.005-0.02 threshold. Gated is the only family showing complementary per-class behaviour. Its trend (#3 better than #9) points towards less regularisation. This trial tests the open question of whether a lighter-regularised gated model can turn that complementarity into a clear gain: weight decay 0.01 instead of 0.1, hidden 64 instead of 32, and the same PCA 64, dropout 0.5 and 200 epochs.
EXPECTED: If capacity was the limit, AUROC should reach about 0.83-0.84 while Cribriform and Papillary stay high and Lepidic and Acinar recover. If it scores at or below 0.823 with larger fold SD, gated fusion is overfit or noise-limited at n=134. I would then drop gated and spend the remaining trials on a few structurally different late or early options before accepting that fusion does not clearly beat H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far is within noise of trial #1 (early, C=0.001, balanced blocks; 0.829), which only matches H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). Early fusion has a sharp C optimum at 0.001; C=0.0001 underfits and C=0.01 is slightly worse. L2 normalisation, PCA32 and block balancing make no clear difference. Gated runs and learned or stacked late fusion are worse, probably from overfitting on 134 patients per fold. Lepidic and Papillary (about 0.72-0.77) are the weak classes.
REASONING: The late fusion trials all used C=0.001, the early-fusion optimum. Averaging three separate models already reduces variance, so each base model may support weaker regularisation. Arithmetic probability averaging (mean_prob) is also untested and is more robust than the geometric mean when one model is overconfident. Late mean_prob at C=0.01 tests whether model diversity plus less-shrunk base learners gives a real gain, and it costs no inner CV.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.83-0.84, possibly with better Papillary and Lepidic. If it again lands at 0.82-0.83, late fusion is no better than early fusion at any reasonable C. I would then conclude that the three embeddings are largely redundant. The remaining budget would go to early-fusion variants: PCA64/128 at C=0.001, or the same at C=0.01.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant so far lands at 0.82-0.83 AUROC, statistically tied with H-optimus-1 alone (0.8297). Early fusion with C=0.001 is the most reliable option, and L2 normalisation, balance_blocks and PCA=32 all made no difference. Late combiners (mean_logit, stack, learned_weights) and the gated network did not beat it, and the gated net overfits. Per-class AUROC is limited by Lepidic (~0.74) and Papillary (~0.72), where the three models fail in much the same way.
REASONING: meta_weight is the one common knob not yet tested; every trial used 1.0. Age/sex carry some independent signal (meta-only AUROC 0.60), and at C=0.001 the two metadata columns are probably shrunk to almost nothing next to thousands of image dimensions. Raising meta_weight to 3 on the accepted best config (#1) isolates that axis cheaply. It is also the only lever left that adds information the foundation models lack, rather than re-mixing redundant embeddings.
EXPECTED: Possible small gain (~+0.005) driven by In situ / Lepidic, where age may matter. If it is flat or worse, I will conclude that metadata adds nothing beyond the image embeddings. In that case the fusion ceiling is set by redundancy between the models, and I will try a few final probes (early with PCA=16 or 64 at matched C, late stack with low stack_C) before accepting that fusion does not clearly beat H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant falls within ±0.01 of the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8297). Early fusion with C=0.001 is the most robust option. Its neighbours (L2 norm, block balancing, meta_weight, PCA32/C=0.01) all land at 0.827-0.829, so the space looks flat around that point. Late combiners, stacking and gated networks did not help, and gated was consistently worse. Papillary (~0.72) and Lepidic (~0.74) are the weak classes for every method.
REASONING: The main untested regime is strong low-rank compression with weaker L2 shrinkage: PCA16 per model, giving 48 features plus meta, with C=0.1. This regularises by dimensionality rather than by ridge shrinkage. It could reduce the noise that limits Papillary and Lepidic separation with only 134 training patients per fold. It is also a qualitatively different point, not another tiny step around trial #1.
EXPECTED: If low-rank structure carries the signal, I expect AUROC around 0.835 or higher with better Papillary and Lepidic scores. If it lands at 0.82-0.83 or below, I will conclude that dimensionality reduction adds nothing over ridge regularisation. Fusion then gives little over H-optimus-1 alone, and the remaining budget should go only to a few distinct checks, such as late fusion with PCA or the weighted_vote combiner.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far sits at or just below 0.829 AUROC, which is the level of H-optimus-1 alone (0.8297). Early fusion is flat across L2 normalisation, meta_weight and balance_blocks, and is best at C≈0.001; PCA and larger C do not help. Gated is consistently worse, so it is overfitting. Late fusion with mean_prob at C=0.01 tied the best, while learned_weights and stack (stack_C=0.1) lost ground, with stack showing poor BA.
REASONING: Per-class patterns differ across methods: stack is best on Lepidic (0.78) and gated is best on Cribriform (0.85-0.86). This hints at class-specific complementarity, which only a stacker can exploit. The earlier stack likely suffered from noisy inner-CV meta-features and too weak shrinkage. Trial #13 showed C=0.01 base models are good for late fusion. Pairing those base models with a stronger-regularised stacker (stack_C=0.01) is the one untested direction that could plausibly give a clear gain, rather than another small knob tweak of early fusion.
EXPECTED: Expect AUROC around 0.83-0.84, with Lepidic kept near 0.78 and BA recovering above 0.42. If it again lands at or below 0.829, that is evidence that per-class reweighting adds nothing over averaging. I would then treat the three embeddings as largely redundant (fusion ≈ best single model) and finish with only a few low-cost checks (e.g. late mean_prob with PCA) before letting the stop rule end the search.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion sits at about 0.82-0.836 AUROC, matching the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.830). Early fusion is flat across L2, meta_weight, balance_blocks and PCA; C=0.001 is optimal. Late stacking (#16, stack_C=0.01, base C=0.01) gave the highest raw score, 0.8358. It lifted Lepidic and Papillary, but its acceptance threshold is large (0.0197) because per-fold variance is high, and its balanced accuracy (BA) is low. The gated method has consistently been worse.
REASONING: Stacking is the only lever that has moved the per-class pattern (Lepidic 0.80, Papillary 0.75). A stronger-shrinkage stacker (stack_C=0.001) should cut the fold-to-fold variance that inflates the threshold, while keeping the base C=0.01 that worked in #16 and #13. This tests whether the stacking gain is real and can be made stable.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.835 with a lower fold SD, ideally clearing the threshold. If it drops or stays unaccepted, the stacking gain is noise or too unstable to rely on, and fusion likely cannot beat H-optimus-1 beyond noise. I would then try one stack variant with l2_normalize or meta_weight before concluding.

ANALYSIS: Most fusions sit on a plateau of about 0.82-0.83, statistically tied with H-optimus-1 alone (0.8297). Early fusion is insensitive to L2 normalisation, block balancing, meta_weight and PCA, and its best C is 0.001. Gated fusion overfits. The only signal above the plateau is the stack combiner with base C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01 (0.8358, Lepidic 0.80, Papillary 0.75). It was not accepted because stacking adds per-fold variance (threshold about 0.02). With base C=0.01, stack_C=0.001 (0.8281) was worse than stack_C=0.01.
REASONING: Stacking is the one direction that changed per-class behaviour, with clearly better Lepidic and Papillary scores. With base C=0.01, stack_C has been tried only at 0.001 and 0.01. Trying stack_C=0.1 checks whether weaker second-level regularisation keeps or extends the gain. A less shrunk meta-learner may also recover balanced accuracy, which is low at 0.38-0.41 with heavily shrunk stacks. This is one cheap trial that maps an open part of the space where a clear gain is plausible.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.835-0.845, with Lepidic and Papillary kept near 0.80 and 0.75 and balanced accuracy closer to 0.43. If the gain exceeds the threshold of about 0.02 it is accepted. If AUROC falls back to about 0.83 or below, the 0.8358 result was a noisy peak. I would then conclude that stacking cannot beat the plateau reliably and move to lower-variance late variants (for example mean_logit at C=0.01) before accepting that fusion offers no clear gain over H-optimus-1.

ANALYSIS: Nearly every fusion lands at 0.82-0.83 AUROC, which is the same as H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). Early fusion is flat across L2 norm, meta_weight and balance_blocks, and is best at C=0.001. Gated networks underperform. Only stacking (C=0.01, stack_C=0.01; #16) showed a meaningful mean gain (+0.007), helped by Lepidic 0.80 and Papillary 0.75. It still failed because its fold-to-fold variance makes the threshold about 0.02.
REASONING: Stacking is the only direction with a plausible clear gain. Its problem is variance, not the mean. Per-slide L2 normalisation of the base models is untested for late fusion. It could stabilise base-model probabilities across folds, reducing the variance of the paired gain and lowering the threshold. I keep the best stack settings (C=0.01, stack_C=0.01) and change only l2_normalize.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.835-0.84 with a smaller gain SE, ideally clearing the threshold. If it again lands near 0.836 with a threshold around 0.02, the stacking gain cannot be separated from noise at n=167. I would then conclude that fusion adds little over H-optimus-1 alone, and stop chasing small differences.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants sit at 0.82-0.836 AUROC. That is indistinguishable from the best single model, H-optimus-1 at 0.830, and from trial #1 at 0.829. Stacking at stack_C=0.01 gave the highest mean (0.836), but its acceptance threshold is around 0.02 because its fold variance is large, so it cannot be accepted. Early fusion is flat across L2 normalisation, block balancing and meta_weight. C=0.001 is the optimum: 0.01 is slightly worse and 0.0001 is clearly worse. The gated model is consistently worse.
REASONING: Six trials remain before the stop rule. The best remaining chance is a variance-reducing change on the strongest family, not a new noisy one. Late fusion with mean_prob at C=0.01 matched the best (0.8298) with a low threshold (0.0046), but C=0.001 is the optimum for early fusion and is untested for mean_prob. Logit averaging at C=0.001 (trial #2) scored lower. Probability averaging of three well-regularised per-model classifiers may calibrate better and add small but consistent per-fold gains. Low fold-to-fold variance of the paired difference is what lets a gain clear the threshold.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.830-0.835, with a paired gain over #1 that is small but consistent, possibly above the threshold of about 0.005. If it is not accepted, the evidence would say that fusing these three models gives no detectable gain over early fusion or H-optimus-1 alone at this sample size. The remaining trials would then be used only to check stacking with meta_weight or PCA before concluding that fusion is saturated.

ANALYSIS: Nothing has beaten the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.8297), by a clear margin. Early fusion peaks at C=0.001 (0.829) and is flat across L2, meta_weight and balance_blocks. The gated network is consistently worse. Stacking (#16, 0.836) has the highest mean, but its high variance makes the threshold about 0.02, so it is hard to accept. For late fusion, raising C from 0.001 to 0.01 helped both mean_prob (0.822→0.830) and mean_logit-type combiners.
REASONING: Late mean_prob has a low-variance paired gain, with a threshold of about 0.005. So a modest real improvement could actually be accepted, unlike with stacking. Its C trend is still rising and C=0.1 is untested. Each per-model regressor sees only one model's features, so it may want weaker regularisation than early fusion does. This trial tests whether the late-fusion optimum lies at higher C.
EXPECTED: AUROC about 0.832–0.836 with a small threshold, which could be accepted. If it drops below 0.829, the late-fusion optimum is at C=0.01. In that case all simple fusions plateau near the H-optimus-1 baseline, and only stack variants are left to try.

ANALYSIS: All fusion methods sit at ~0.82-0.83 AUROC, statistically indistinguishable from the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297) and from trial #1. Late stacking with stack_C=0.01 gave the highest raw score (0.8358), but its corrected SE threshold is large (~0.02), so it cannot be accepted. Early fusion is flat across C in 0.001-0.01, L2 norm, meta_weight and balance_blocks. Gated fusion is consistently worse. Only 4 trials remain before the stop rule triggers.
REASONING: With so few trials left, the only lever that has not been tested is early fusion with PCA 64 or 128 per model at C=0.001. This might denoise the 1536-2560-d blocks while keeping more signal than PCA 32 or 16. PCA 128 with C=0.001 is a modest, plausible variant. Alternatively, mean_logit at C=0.01 could match mean_prob. None of these is likely to clear the threshold, though. The PCA option does answer an open question: does moderate dimensionality reduction help early fusion at the best C?
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of about 0.825-0.832, which would be rejected. If so, I conclude that fusion gives no detectable gain over trial #1 or H-optimus-1 alone at n=167. The remaining budget should end the search rather than chase noise, and trial #1 should be reported as roughly equivalent to the best single model.

ANALYSIS: Early fusion at C=0.001 (0.829) only matches H-optimus-1 alone (0.830). It is flat across L2 norm, balance_blocks, meta_weight and PCA. Gated fusion is consistently worse. Late stacking with stack_C=0.01 gives the highest mean (0.836), with Lepidic and Papillary gains. However, its paired-gain SE is large (threshold about 0.02), so no stack trial has been accepted. stack_C=0.1 overfits and 0.001 underfits, so stack_C=0.01 is the sweet spot.
REASONING: With 3 trials left before the stop rule, the only signal worth pursuing is the stack at stack_C=0.01. It has been tested only with base C=0.01. Base learners at C=0.001 were the best regularisation for early fusion and give smoother, better-calibrated inner-CV log-probabilities. That should make the meta-learner less noisy per fold and could both raise the mean and shrink the gain SE. This is the one untested combination that plausibly clears the threshold.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.835-0.84 with lower fold-to-fold variance than trial #16, possibly enough to be accepted. If it lands at or below about 0.83, or is rejected again, the conclusion is that stacking's apparent gain is within noise. In that case no fusion clearly beats H-optimus-1 alone on 167 patients, and trial #1 (equivalent to the best single model) should be reported.

ANALYSIS: Every method plateaus around 0.82-0.836 AUROC. Early fusion (#1, 0.829) roughly matches the best single model, H-optimus-1 (0.830). The highest mean, 0.8358 from late stack at C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01 (#16), came with a large corrected threshold (~0.02). That variance comes from the inner-CV stacker, so the +0.007 gain is indistinguishable from noise. Gated is consistently worse, and L2 norm, meta_weight and balance_blocks have negligible effects.
REASONING: With two trials left before the stop rule, the most promising region is the #16 stacker, which raised Lepidic and Papillary AUROC. Its problem is fold-to-fold variance, not its mean. PCA=64 per model should make the base learners' inner-CV log-probabilities less noisy and more consistent. That could reduce the variance of the paired gain and therefore lower the acceptance threshold. It also tests whether PCA interacts with stacking, which has not been tried.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.833-0.838 with a smaller fold SD and a threshold below ~0.015, which might allow acceptance. If it is rejected again, I would conclude that fusion gains over early concatenation are within noise. The defensible final choice would then be the simple, low-variance early fusion of #1, or simply H-optimus-1 alone.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion method lands at 0.82-0.836 AUROC, which is roughly equal to the best single model (H-optimus-1, 0.8297). Early fusion is flat across C near 0.001, L2 normalisation, PCA, balance_blocks and meta_weight. Gated networks underperform. Only stacking with base C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01 shows a consistent positive trend (+0.005 to +0.007; Lepidic and Papillary improve). Its per-fold gains vary too much to clear the roughly 0.02 threshold, and balanced accuracy drops.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires, so it should go to the only signal that repeats across runs: stacking with C=0.01 and stack_C=0.01. Stronger dimensionality reduction (PCA 32) on the base models may make the inner-CV log-probabilities less noisy. That could reduce fold-to-fold variance of the gain, which is what currently sets the threshold. PCA 64 (#24) and no PCA (#16) are already done, so PCA 32 is the untested neighbour.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.833-0.838 with a somewhat lower SD of the per-fold gain. Acceptance is possible but unlikely. If it is rejected, I conclude that with 167 patients, fusing these three models gives no reliable gain over the best single model or simple early fusion. In that case I would report trial #1 (or H-optimus-1 alone) and not tune further on noise.
